title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Implementing the Protective Clause in Consular Treaties When Taking Compulsory Measures Against Ships of the Sending State

articles.content_en: Article 2. Where a maritime court decides to auction a detained vessel to settle debts, it shall, before issuing the auction notice, provide written notification to the embassy and consulate of the country to which the defendant belongs, located in China.

Article 3. Where a maritime court needs to conduct a formal investigation on board a vessel of a contracting state due to maritime or maritime commerce disputes, it shall notify in advance the embassy and consulate of the flag state located in China. If the circumstances are urgent and advance notification is not possible, it shall provide written notification immediately after the investigation.

Article 4. When each maritime court takes the actions mentioned above, if, due to urgent circumstances, it notifies the flag state's embassy and consulate in China after the fact, and if the consular officer of that country requests full information regarding the actions taken, the court shall promptly provide such information.

Article 5. The above-mentioned notification shall be submitted by the maritime court to the Higher People's Court of the province or city where it is located for review, and then directly sent to the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which shall then be responsible for forwarding it to the embassy and consulate in China of the vessel's sending state to be notified.

Article 6. When serving the notification, the civil ruling on detaining the vessel or the civil ruling on compulsory auction of the detained vessel and the service receipt shall be attached.

(2) Status of consular treaties concluded by China
Appendix (2)
Status of consular treaties concluded by China
(I) The other contracting states of the consular treaties that have taken effect are:
United States, Yugoslavia, Poland, North Korea, Hungary, Italy, Cuba, Russia (succeeding the original Sino-Soviet Consular Treaty), Mexico, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Laos, Lithuania, Argentina, Tunisia, Turkey, Iraq, Romania, India, Mongolia, Slovakia (succeeding the original Sino-Czech Consular Treaty), Croatia (applying the original Sino-Yugoslav Consular Treaty), Slovenia (applying the original Sino-Yugoslav Consular Treaty).
(II) The other contracting states of the consular treaties that have not yet taken effect are:
Kazakhstan, Pakistan, Moldova, Bolivia, Ukraine, Yemen, Turkmenistan, Belarus.
